I really want to like this game but there are so many little annoyances. The talent tree will generate dead ends, which can completely kill a run on higher difficulties. The class balance is whack, with the starter class being next to impossible to lose on period on any difficulty, with the rest lagging a mile behind feeling kind of ♥♥♥♥ to play with (usually) dinky range, glacial attack speed, and much more limited ability usage until 75% of the way through a run, if you can make it that far. The talent packs which give a set of abilities on the tree range from stupidly strong to "your run is now over because this was a win more pack, not a start to win pack". Sometimes the central talent to a pack generates across a gap in the tree, also functionally ending your run. Every class has "challenges" which are usually easy and pretty brain dead and unlock a legendary talent you will likely never see, or a skin that (imo) looks worse than the default. I might come back and give it a shot again the future, and it does only cost $4 for ~10 hours of entertainment, but the cracks start to show and the fun melts away once you start moving the difficulty up for most classes

This game is mediocre. Runs take too long to get going, and end just as your build starts doing something. After winning you unlock 1 or 2 mastery levels, of which there are 25 (35?), the first 10 or so mastery levels being easy to the point that there is no strategy or skill expression of any kind. Not that there are any later, as you either get good perks early, and it's free, or you don't, and there is nothing you can do. This is where the game starts to crack and show its flaws. "Choose your upgrades and abilities wisely and you might just make it out alive." You have very little control over your build. You choose one of the two or three visible perks or abilities in the talent tree, and make your way towards it. You have to take the nodes that lead to whatever you pick, hoping they're not useless. There is also a chance you stumble upon a dead end, because most of the tree is hidden behind a fog. You pick "wisely" from your limited options, and you "might just make it out alive" if you are lucky. The premise of the game is flawed at best, and deceptive at worst. I cannot recommend this game to anyone, even on sale. Final note for my fellow achievements hunters: Unlocking all the mastery levels, and doing all the challenges seems very grindy and RNG dependent. Getting 100% achievements requires buying DLCs, which at the time of this review triples the price of the game.
